sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova: A New Generation of Foundation Models
sources.evidence: December 3, 2024 announcement expressly says Nova Micro, Lite and Pro are generally available that day. Identifies Amazon as developer and Nova as the family, with Lite accepting text, image and video and producing text.

sources.title: Nova Lite - Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Exact amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 card documents 300K context, text/image/video input, text output and client-side tool calling. Calls it a low-cost multimodal model for document analysis and visual Q&A. Its December 5, 2024 launch date conflicts with the contemporaneous December 3 GA announcement.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Section 1.1, page 3 explicitly identifies Pro, Lite and Micro as Transformer-based, and describes Lite's multimodal inputs and agentic capabilities. No total/active parameter counts or dense/MoE topology are provided. Web extraction exceeded its size limit; the publisher PDF was successfully streamed through pdftotext and inspected.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: April 30, 2025 addendum names Lite among distillation students. Checked the later report and comparison tables; they do not disclose Lite's parameter counts or dense/MoE topology.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: December 2, 2025 report includes Nova 1 Lite rows in benchmark comparison tables. Those rows do not supply total/active parameters or dense/MoE topology; Nova 2 specifications are not transferred to Nova 1 Lite.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Premier - AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: Service card scoped to April 30, 2025 models identifies Lite within the Nova family, its modalities, fast processing and Transformer-based inference. It does not state total/active parameters or dense/MoE topology.

sources.title: Customize Amazon Nova in Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: July 16, 2025 announcement expressly calls Nova a proprietary model family and names Micro, Lite and Pro as the models covered by its customization offering.

sources.title: Available foundation models - Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: Inventory dated July 29, 2026 lists Nova Lite (nova-textgeneration-lite) with license AWS Service Terms. The row appears under an Open-Weight Models heading, conflicting with Nova-specific proprietary classification and escrow documentation; the broad heading alone is not treated as a weight-release announcement.

sources.title: Migrate from Amazon Nova 1 to Amazon Nova 2 on Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: March 18, 2026 comparison explicitly gives Nova 1 Lite 300K context, text/image/video input and Extended Thinking = No. It maps the first generation to amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 and describes extended thinking as an addition in Nova 2.

sources.title: Iterative Training - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current documentation explicitly states Nova weights are proprietary and customized checkpoints remain in escrow buckets in AWS-managed accounts instead of being copied into the customer's account. Examples use Nova 2; this corroborates the exact first-generation classification in s7 rather than independently identifying Lite v1.

sources.title: Models.dev Nova Lite v1 source record
sources.evidence: Followed the baseline link. It identifies its metadata as carried over from the OpenRouter provider catalog; it is a discovery source, not primary verification of model specifications.

sources.title: Complete request schema - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current Nova user-guide schema explicitly labels reasoningConfig as applicable to Nova Pro and Nova Lite, with enabled/disabled and low/medium/high effort. This conflicts with the March 2026 exact Nova 1 Lite migration table. The schema does not include an exact Lite API identifier.

sources.title: Using the Converse API - Amazon Nova Version 1
sources.evidence: Page explicitly labels itself Version 1, maps Nova Lite to amazon.nova-lite-v1:0, and documents function calling and image/video inputs. It describes topK but no reasoningConfig or extended-thinking capability; absence here does not by itself prove unsupported reasoning.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Version 1 model specifications
sources.evidence: Exact amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 column lists PDF document support. The migration guide states document input remains Converse-only.

name.note: Retain the display name for official Nova Lite / Nova 1 Lite, mapped to amazon.nova-lite-v1:0; this is not Nova 2 Lite.

developer.note: Amazon's launch and its AGI-authored technical report establish developer identity.

family.note: Normalize to the developer's Nova family; Lite is a member/tier rather than a separate family.

release_date.note: Use earliest explicit public GA on December 3. The current Bedrock card's December 5 launch date is retained as a source conflict, not substituted for the contemporaneous release.

open_weights.note: Developer explicitly calls the exact first-generation family proprietary; current Nova docs explain proprietary weights remain in AWS escrow. JumpStart's broad Open-Weight heading conflicts, but its Lite row provides no downloadable checkpoint or self-hosting route.

license.note: Exact Nova Lite row labels its license AWS Service Terms. These are proprietary service/model-use terms, not an open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No total count in the original technical report, later Premier addendum, Nova 2 comparisons or service card checked. No benchmark- or pricing-derived estimate is substituted.

active_parameters_b.note: The checked reports do not separately state active parameters or disclose dense/MoE topology; active count cannot be inferred from Transformer architecture.

architecture.note: The original report explicitly says Transformer-based. This records only that disclosed architecture class; dense versus MoE remains undisclosed.

context_window.note: Both the exact Bedrock card and later Nova 1 Lite comparison specify 300K tokens.

modalities.note: Exact card confirms text/image/video to text. Version 1 specifications add PDF document input; document support is through Converse rather than Invoke.

reasoning.note: Unresolved first-party conflict: the March 2026 Nova 1 Lite comparison says Extended Thinking = No, but the current shared request schema expressly assigns reasoningConfig to Nova Lite. The exact v1 Converse page documents no reasoning mode. No endpoint invocation or version-specific update resolves this; clear baseline false rather than claim either value.

tool_call.note: Client-side tool calling is expressly supported; absence of Nova 2 built-in tools does not negate function calling.

description.value: Nova model with text, image, video and PDF input, text output, a 300K-token context and tool calling.
description.note: Summary of documented inputs, output, context and tool calling without speed or price claims.

patch.description: Nova model with text, image, video and PDF input, text output, a 300K-token context and tool calling.
patch.notes: Public GA was announced December 3, 2024; the later Bedrock card lists December 5. Transformer-based is disclosed, but total/active parameter counts and dense/MoE topology are not. AWS Service Terms are proprietary use terms; Nova-specific documentation identifies proprietary weights held in AWS-managed escrow despite the JumpStart inventory's broad Open-Weight heading. Reasoning mode is unresolved: the Nova 1 Lite migration table says no extended thinking, while the current shared Nova request schema assigns reasoningConfig to Lite. PDF input is supported through the Converse API.

summary: Correct release to explicit December 3 public GA, add video input, identify the Nova family, record Transformer-based architecture and AWS Service Terms, and make the description specific. Confirm 300K context and client-side tool calling. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed after checking original and later first-party reports and tables. Clear reasoning to null because exact Nova 1 migration guidance and current shared schema conflict. Record the conflicting December 5 listing and JumpStart inventory heading; specific Nova documentation supports proprietary weights. Parent review also verified and added PDF document input from the exact Version 1 model column.
